architecture_fit_summary: Good fit for Redwood Private VPC: customer wants single-tenant control plane, VPC peering to vendor-managed subnets, egress-controlled NAT, and BYOK integration with AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault. Primary constraint: PHI must remain in US regions and audit logs must be exported to Splunk/Hadoop. Performance targets (p95 latency < 120ms for chat; throughput 500 concurrent sessions) appear achievable with dedicated GPU pool + prefix caching. Need to validate network ACLs and approved regions with customer security team.
notes:
- Company handles medical claims + patient chat assistants (PHI scope).
- Quote from Head of Infra: "BYOK and explicit egress control are non-negotiable."
- Security cares about audit log retention 7 years; wants Splunk ingestion and immutable logs.
- Prefer AWS us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 for DR; EU regions not allowed for PHI.
- Proposed topology: vendor-managed subnets for inference nodes, VPC peering to customer VPC, private endpoints for S3 and KMS, NAT gateway for controlled egress, optional transit gateway for multi-account setup.
- Inbound: no public ingress to inference nodes; control plane APIs via private endpoints and mutual TLS + IP allowlist.
- Outbound: restricted to specific SaaS endpoints (identity, observability), all other egress blocked.
- KMS: customer wants BYOK with rotating CMKs and HSM-backed keys; require integration guide + automated key rotation demo.
- Compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001 required, also state-level HIPAA readiness checklist requested.
- Cost sensitivity: high at scale; they want detailed cost modeling for dedicated vs hosted + caching/quantization savings.
- POC ask: 2-week pilot with sandbox dataset (de-identified) then 6-week production proof with real PHI behind VPC.
- Stated blocker: procurement wants procurement vs subscription firm analysis; legal wants DPA + embassy clause for BYOK.
- Action items for AE/SE: provide hardened VPC reference diagram, list of exact egress IPs/domains, KMS BYOK runbook, SLA language draft.
- Useful refs: pricing deck (drive), security-faq doc, previous enterprise BYOK runbook (internal).
